correctness.rationale: A one-point diagram is determined by a lower ideal L and upper filter U that are disjoint and satisfy L<U elementwise. These conditions are exactly the necessary and sufficient transitivity conditions; finite extension and homogeneity over named parameters identify such diagrams with complete nonalgebraic types. Profiles with one side empty number 2i(G)-1 for the retained graph G, since ideals and filters correspond to independent sets by complementing one shore. When both sides are nonempty they must lie in A and B respectively and span only retained comparisons, giving i(F)-2^a-2^b+1. The mixed independent sets of G are exactly bicliques in the missing graph F, so tau=i(F)+2^a+2^b-2+2q(F). Fair independent vertex choices give edge-avoidance probability 3/4; decreasing events are positively associated, including intersections of edge-avoidance events. In a nonmatching graph choose a wedge: its joint avoidance probability is 5/8 (center absent with probability 1/2, or center alone among those three with probability 1/8). Grouping it before correlation gives the exact improved bound on i(F); substitution adds 3^(k-2)2^(a+b-2k) above the matching baseline. Each edge contributes one biclique, each adjacent edge pair a distinct additional biclique, so equality in the first bound forces a matching and equality in the second forces exactly one adjacent pair. This is precisely one two-edge star plus k-2 disjoint edges, which attains equality by component factorization and has sufficient vertices on both shores. At k=0 or 1 the first equality condition is automatic and the second is not asserted; at a=b=k=2 the matching and star values are 19 and 22. Setting a=b=k=n and comparing with k=0 gives the stated standard-example ratio.
residual_risks: The packaged 255-case closure check is recorded corroboration, not an independent run and not needed for the exact all-parameter argument. Equality is of structural forms, not of a unique placement of named vertices.

originality.rationale: The established general height-two identity, local one-edge sensitivities and known count at a matching are not independent contributions. The supported distinct result is the sharp optimization over all fixed-size deletion patterns, notably the exact second attainable value and its complete equality class. Harris association is standard; using the precise joint wedge gap and the rigidity of the biclique term gives the new extremal comparison. The inspected statements did not give this optimization or a stronger statement with both sharp bounds and equality cases.
residual_risks: No date-based priority is assigned between same-day records. A stronger published sparse extremal independent-set classification was not confirmed by this bounded search and remains possible.

value.rationale: Over a natural two-level family this classifies exactly how distributing the same deletion budget changes the space of possible one-point extensions. The first departure from optimality already has a quantified cost and a rigid equality configuration. This turns a known local counting law into a sharp global comparison of independent and interacting defects, not just a computation of the standard example.
residual_risks: The type count does not reconstruct the parameter poset; the theorem does not optimize over arbitrary partial orders or k above the matching-feasibility threshold.
